motivation: Replace repeated full-field Fermat equality tests in the private fixed-scan index query with exact membership indicators on the known valid locator support
precondition: Valid starting state: N distinct database locators; each valid index occurrence equals one of them; invalid occurrences have zero slot flag. Probe coordinates are bits, so each block has exactly one secret one-hot bucket flag. The existing state invariant and trusted binary query interface establish these conditions.
identity: L_j(x)=product_{i!=j}(x-h_i)/product_{i!=j}(h_j-h_i). On the valid locator set, this is exactly1 at h_j and0 at other h_i. Invalid-slot factors are suppressed by the zero flag.
algorithm: Compute nonzero denominator inverses once per query by exact exponentp-2. Use a balanced product tree and its complementary products for all leave-one-out products on public-size slot batches. Reduce factors1-slot_flag*L_j(x) per database row.
variants: secretly select the query bucket in every block, then polynomial membership on BLOCKS*C slots
compose bucket selection with the virtual-epoch transition
bucket_selection: Read every original padded slot; choose one bucket per block by secret one-hot flags. Public-size oblivious arithmetic; no access-pattern or candidate-count opening.
correctness: Compare complete candidate flags with the original exact field-equality implementation inside DIAG, plus independent Hamming/label oracle. Include synthetic no-match, all-match/tie and selective-match fixtures as correctness-only tests, and real frozen CelebA roots for performance.
key_comparison: N8 D512; eager original vs full-index polynomial vs bucket-selected polynomial; one warmup and five repetitions in balanced order
scale: Bucket-selected variant N32/N128 D512, one warmup/three repetitions. These are measured scale points without a baseline speedup claim at those sizes.
security_boundary: Same passive five-party Shamir and hidden index/locators. No new openings. Distinct-handle and valid-state preconditions must be explicit; this is not malicious-input validation.
claim: Lagrange interpolation/product trees are established mathematics. Any novelty claim must concern the useful system contract and evaluation, not invention of polynomial membership.
scheduling: After current AES series, before CPU-heavy frontend work, using the shared runtime lock
